_readme: Taste markers: what in a book moves the reader's score, and by how much. Each book's markers and their strengths (1 minor, 2 clear, 3 central) live in book-taste.jsonl, set by screening; the reader's reviews live in book-reviews.json. The estimate is the baseline plus each marker's effect, and the effects are fitted from the reviews, pulled toward `prior`. Nothing here is per-title.
_kind: veto: the book is blocked whatever else it has, the rulebook's hard filters. graded: adds `prior` points at strength 3, scaled by `shape` at strengths 1 and 2.
_prior: Points on 0-100 at strength 3 before any review moves it. Taken from book-recommendations.md: a stated convention where it gives one (`stated`), else read off its anchors (`anchored`), else a guess at the direction only (`unmeasured`).
_shape: Share of the full effect at strengths 1, 2, 3. Default [0.33, 0.67, 1].

markers.label: real-world occult
markers.use: A system drawn from actual occultism or real gods, on the page: witchcraft or spellcasting in that mould, seance, divination, necromancy, demon-summoning from grimoire tradition, prayer or sacrifice to real deities. Resemblance counts. Not an engineered system with declared rules and no invocation.

markers.label: human sacrifice staged
markers.use: A human sacrifice the narrative stages, by anyone, heroes included. Origin lore that is only told is invented-rite instead.

markers.label: detective or mystery novel
markers.use: The book's satisfaction is solving a crime or who did it. An investigation subplot inside another kind of book is not this.

markers.label: infidelity as the premise
markers.use: Remove an affair inside a marriage or engagement and there is no book. Not an arranged betrothal, not unmarried partners. When premise versus subplot is unclear, use infidelity-subplot.

markers.label: sex as the plot
markers.use: The plot is mainly about sexual behaviour or a sexual relationship: remove the sex and there is no book.

markers.label: same-sex relationship of a lead
markers.use: The protagonist, or a lead whose strand the book follows, has a same-sex romance or sexual relationship, on the page or as backstory the plot turns on. When it is unclear whose it is or whether it is one, use same-sex-secondary.

markers.label: opening switches before investing
markers.use: The opening leaves its first strand for another before any strand has hooked. Several viewpoints are fine when each invests before the next arrives.

markers.label: opening without context
markers.source: Caropisci: abandoned cold at chapter one, only a few points off with the premise read first ('still around 80'). Propose with a read-the-premise-first note.
markers.use: Dropped into action already underway with no context: who the people are, what the invented terms mean and why it matters are not established. 3 when the first chapters stay like that.

markers.label: early stall
markers.source: Four deep dives predicted 8-9 and put down part-way: Permafrost, Zaslana posta 60, Strepy Zeme, Vydech 60.
markers.use: An early stretch where nothing invests: exposition-heavy first part, leads left unexplained, a slack run after chapter one. A stall reviewers note and push through still counts.

markers.label: invented rite staged
markers.source: Convention light -2, moderate -5, heavy -10 (rulebook, occult filter).
markers.use: A rite of an invented system enacted on the page. 1 light: an incidental ceremony that does nothing. 2 moderate: a rite that works, staged once or twice. 3 heavy: rites central to the plot or to how the leads' power works, or raising the dead; also sacrifice told as a power system's origin.

markers.label: men dumb, women clever
markers.source: Convention mild -2, moderate -5, strong -10. Anchor Caropisci 50, mild.
markers.use: A one-sided competence contrast: men shown as dumb or incompetent while women are shown as good or clever, with no in-world reason. 1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 strong.

markers.label: crude sexual content
markers.source: Ready Player One 40 ('the kind of sex'), Artemis 50 (crude in small doses).
markers.use: Sexual references or scenes treated crudely. Judge what the book is crude about, not a coarse voice.

markers.label: much sexual content
markers.source: Volume is real but unmeasured; Valka stareho muze 87 shows one chapter registers.
markers.use: How much of the book is sexual content, whatever its treatment. 1 a scene or a chapter, 3 throughout.

markers.label: infidelity below premise
markers.source: Reader's stated bands: approving incidental in the 50s, neutral subplot 45-55, approving subplot 30-40. No read book anchors it.
markers.use: An affair inside a marriage or engagement that is not the premise. Strength is prominence and approval together: 1 incidental and condemned, 3 an approving subplot.

markers.label: same-sex relationship off the leads
markers.source: Graded below the leads; magnitude unmeasured.
markers.use: A secondary character's same-sex relationship, a background couple, a passing mention, or an unclear case.

markers.label: religion played as satire
markers.source: Ja, robot 50, which carries two other causes.
markers.use: Religion or faith ridiculed or played for cynicism. Not political or social satire.

markers.label: theology as the subject
markers.source: Stated directly that a theology book is not wanted.
markers.use: Theology or apologetics as the book's subject rather than a thread inside a story.

markers.label: flat lead
markers.source: Artemis 50 against Project Hail Mary 100, same author, world-logic fine.
markers.use: A lead with no interiority or one note, shown in the text. Ordinary is not flat: never set this for an everyman or a generic-sounding lead.

markers.label: no one to root for
markers.source: Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes 50 against Sunrise on the Reaping 87.
markers.use: The lead acts as a villain or slides into evil, or nobody in the story is worth rooting for. A dark past faced and refused is not this.

markers.label: passive lead
markers.source: Promena 40, Problem tri teles (DNF), Oliver Twist 50.
markers.use: The lead is acted upon rather than wanting and doing anything.

markers.label: unearned competence
markers.source: Divergent 50.
markers.use: Ability and status given rather than earned; effortlessly good at everything.

markers.label: world or plot doesn't hold up
markers.source: Mortal Engines 50, Divergent 50, Unfinished Tales 50; can end a book in the first chapters.
markers.use: The author breaks rules he laid down: a declared capability without consequences, an explanation that fails, a society that does not cohere, rescue by luck, a reveal sprung rather than earned, false real-world claims, parts that do not connect. Strength is how central and how wrong.

markers.label: sustained bleakness
markers.source: 1984 60 against Animal Farm 78; the full-strength case gives back about 10 points.
markers.use: The book's mood is isolation, hopelessness or unrelieved grimness. Not violence, a bleak ending or a dark subject told at a distance.

markers.label: padding and digression
markers.source: LOTR 84 capped by sparse story, Zaslana posta 60, Les Miserables 71, Monte Cristo 60.
markers.use: A thin story spread over many pages: description, digression, drawn-out endings. Never length itself.

markers.label: little drive to read on
markers.source: Pocitani hvezd 80, its one named problem.
markers.use: Stretches where nothing pulls the reader forward, beyond the opening.

markers.label: events over people
markers.source: Golden Son 92 docked for leaning on action; Strepy Zeme (DNF) 'only something like scifi history'.
markers.use: Page time goes to set-piece action, description or a world's history with no person's wants on the page.

markers.label: unconnected collection
markers.source: Ja, robot 50, Vydech 60: read from the front, put down on weak early pieces.
markers.use: A collection of separate stories or pieces. 3 for a multi-author or best-of anthology, 1 for an arc or fix-up where each piece builds on the last.

markers.label: verse
markers.source: Havran 10, the form named as the first cause.
markers.use: Written in verse. 3 for a whole book of poetry.

markers.label: children's register
markers.source: Picture books in the 30s-40s; Hranicaruv ucen 50-70 and Narnia 60 pay; The Hobbit 84 and The Little Prince 82 do not.
markers.use: How juvenile the telling is when there is no adult layer for it to grade. 1 a crossover with an adult layer, 3 a picture book or age-banded serial.

markers.label: lead feels like a child
markers.source: Ender's Game 87, docked slightly.
markers.use: The lead's inner life reads as a child's. Not the stated age.

markers.label: sequel re-runs book one
markers.source: Catching Fire 83 against Mockingjay 91; Osudove nebe set aside; Hitchhiker's sequels 50.
markers.use: A sequel that repeats or escalates book one's premise instead of opening a new question.

markers.label: discovery under necessity
markers.source: Convention: central +4, partial +2. Project Hail Mary 100, Licanius 93-100.
markers.use: An unknown world or past the lead must explore to survive or finish his task, with the outcome open until an answer that fits. 3 when it is the spine, 1-2 partial. Not a mystery the book refuses to answer.

markers.label: ideas to think about
markers.source: Licanius 96, Seeking Allah 100, The Little Prince 82 against Narnia 60 and Hranicaruv ucen for lacking them.
markers.use: The book leaves an idea to think about and grow from, handled without forcing or mocking it, and you can name it in a sentence.

markers.label: belief taken seriously
markers.source: Licanius 93-100 ('not forced or mocking anything'), Seeking Allah 100.
markers.use: Faith, fate or belief questioned seriously as a thread inside the story.

markers.label: interesting lead
markers.source: Red Rising 95, Stin veci ztracenych 93 (a past being uncovered), Valka stareho muze 87 (ordinary, written well).
markers.use: Inner life and motives on the page, flaws to overcome, a past worth uncovering.

markers.label: someone to root for
markers.source: Project Hail Mary 100 (Rocky, sacrifice) against The Martian 82; LOTR 84.
markers.use: Someone worth rooting for and something good to hold on to: friendship, self-sacrifice, hope.

markers.label: people over events
markers.source: Mockingjay 91 > Hunger Games 89 > Catching Fire 83; Project Hail Mary 100 > The Martian 82.
markers.use: Page time on what the characters want and why.

markers.label: characters think differently
markers.source: Golden Son 92 (Darrow, Sevro, Mustang).
markers.use: Each character has their own motives and way of thinking. Not cast size.

markers.label: world and plot hold up
markers.source: Project Hail Mary 100, Golden Son 92, Licanius 93-100, Valka stareho muze 87.
markers.use: Declared rules kept and their consequences carried, reveals that fit what came before, nobody rescued by luck. For a real-world book, true to how things are.

markers.label: fast start, constant pull
markers.source: Red Rising 95, Hunger Games 89, Ender's Game 87.
markers.use: Clear and gripping from page one, and never drags.
